tone_patterns: Uses formal, institutional language with an emphasis on strategic intent and alignment to recognised standards.
Balances value-creation framing (long-term value, risk diversification) with sustainability framing (ESG integration, responsible finance).
Employs explanatory, definitional tone when introducing products or services, often clarifying how items are classified or measured for reporting.
Uses cautious, process-oriented phrasing (e.g., progressive improvement, careful evaluation) rather than absolute claims.
paragraph_patterns: Opens subsections with a short positioning statement describing how sustainability is embedded in a business line or function.
Follows with a policy/approach description that explains governance of the strategy (e.g., guided by principles, institutionalised through a policy).
Introduces a structured list of pillars/commitments, then expands with operational details (scope, coverage, applicability).
Includes a paragraph describing engagement mechanisms and escalation options (e.g., meetings, voting, divestment) as part of responsible practices.
Uses product spotlights: short descriptive blocks that define a product, explain its purpose, and describe reporting/measurement treatment.
Concludes subsections with a synthesis paragraph linking initiatives to broader strategic positioning and opportunity capture.
heading_patterns: Uses clear, business-line-specific subheadings (e.g., segment/function + sustainability theme).
Employs title case for headings and keeps them concise.
Places the main section label (Strategy) consistently as a running footer/header element on pages within the section.
Uses descriptive headings for tables that distinguish categories (e.g., on-balance vs off-balance) as separate labeled blocks.
table_patterns: Uses a simple three-column taxonomy table: serial number, product/category label, and a concise description.
Splits a large taxonomy into two consecutive tables by classification (e.g., on-balance sheet vs off-balance sheet) with repeated column headers.
Descriptions in the table reference external frameworks/principles to define eligibility and alignment criteria.
Table entries are written as noun phrases for product names and sentence fragments for descriptions to keep rows compact.
Uses consistent numbering within each table block (restarts numbering per classification).
figure_or_diagram_patterns: Uses a matrix-style product map with multiple vertical columns representing business lines and rows representing product/advisory offerings.
Column headers are short labels; row items are brief phrases, creating a scan-friendly capability overview.
Includes a short narrative paragraph adjacent to or below the matrix to interpret the product suite and connect it to strategic objectives.
Employs callout-style boxes for retail initiatives: each box has a short title and a compact explanatory paragraph.
pdf_layout_patterns: Multi-page section with consistent page footer containing section name, page number, and report title line.
Tables occupy the majority of a page with minimal surrounding narrative when presenting taxonomies.
Uses two-column text blocks for narrative sections, with bullets embedded within the flow for key pillars.
Intermixes narrative paragraphs with structured visual elements (matrix table/diagram) on the same page to break up dense text.
Uses boxed callouts arranged in a grid (e.g., three items) to present multiple initiatives in parallel with equal visual weight.
Maintains clear whitespace between subsections and visual elements to signal transitions.
disclosure_language_patterns: Defines products and policies by referencing recognised market principles and eligibility criteria rather than bespoke definitions.
Clarifies scope and applicability (e.g., which portfolios/mandates are covered) using categorical language.
Explains measurement/reporting approach for advisory/facilitation activities (e.g., how contributions are attributed) to support transparency.
Uses alignment language (aligned with, guided by, structured around) to connect activities to frameworks and internal policies.
Distinguishes between direct financing and facilitation/advisory roles through explicit classification wording.
evidence_presentation_patterns: Supports credibility by citing external standards/principles as the basis for classification and eligibility.
Uses structured lists (pillars/commitments) as quasi-evidence of a systematic approach.
Provides process evidence (engagement methods, escalation steps) rather than outcome evidence in the strategy narrative.
Uses product inventories/taxonomies as evidence of breadth of offerings.
section_specific_observations: Strategy content is organised by business segment/function, each with its own mini-structure: positioning statement → policy/approach → mechanisms → product set.
Sustainable finance is presented through classification schemas (balance-sheet treatment; product families; advisory vs financing).
Retail initiatives are communicated via short, consumer-facing product summaries in visually separated callouts, contrasting with institutional narrative elsewhere.
things_to_avoid_copying: Any company name, subsidiary/department names, or branded product names.
Any references to specific regions, regulators, or jurisdiction-specific claims presented as achievements.
Any numeric thresholds, percentages, dates, or quantified coverage ranges.
Any claims of being first/leading or certification levels and awarding bodies as stated in the excerpt.
Any specific external framework names should not be reproduced verbatim as a template requirement; instead, leave placeholders for applicable frameworks.
content_specific_items_detected_and_excl: Named financial institution and group branding repeated in headers/footers.
Specific sustainable finance frameworks/principles and named standard-setting bodies cited for eligibility/alignment.
Specific product brand names and initiative labels in retail banking callouts.
Jurisdiction/region references and regulatory references tied to particular sectors.
Certification program references and superlative leadership/first-mover statements.
Specific numeric thresholds and time-bound net-zero reference.
